source_evidence: At the end of the year, the fund distributes these capital gains, minus any capital losses, to investors.
answer: A capital gains distribution happens when an ETF distributes gains from securities it sold at a higher price, after subtracting any capital losses. The fund makes these distributions to investors at the end of the year. ETFs typically have fewer capital gains distributions than mutual funds because many ETFs exchange portfolio securities in kind rather than selling them for cash.
